title: SSR Security and Reliability knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “SSR Security and Reliability”?
options: SSR Security and Reliability should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
SSR Security and Reliability helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
SSR Security and Reliability means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
SSR Security and Reliability removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: SSR Security and Reliability helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: SSR Security and Reliability is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Server-side secret handling” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Server-side secret handling” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Server-side secret handling” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Server-side secret handling” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Server-side secret handling” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Server-side secret handling” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Server-side secret handling” under SSR Security and Reliability. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “SSR Security and Reliability”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
